correctness.rationale: For invertible A and generic plane normal U, the unique linear dependence of projected opposite vectors has coefficients c=A^{-1}U. An opposite pair drops from the projected hull iff |c_i|>|c_j|+|c_k|, because the projected image lies strictly inside the diamond conv(±q_j,±q_k). These exclusive dominance chambers subdivide into four positive trihedral cones per index and their antipodes, yielding the 1/(2pi) angle sum. Substitution A=diag(1,1,lambda) gives Omega_x=2 atan((sqrt2-1)lambda/(1+h)) and Omega_z=2 atan((h-lambda)^2), h=sqrt(1+lambda^2), hence the displayed p4. Writing t=asinh(lambda), u=tanh(t/2), a=sqrt2-1, the derivative factors as (pi/4) dp4/dt=(1-u^2)(2-sqrt2)(u^2-a^2)(u^2+3+2sqrt2)/((1+a^2u^2)(1+6u^2+u^4)). Independent SymPy simplified both sides to zero identically. Since u increases through a at lambda=1, the strict minimum is unique and endpoints yield p4->1. The standard solid-angle identity and source theorem cover all positive lambda, not a finite experiment; no assertion on arbitrary nonsymmetric affine optimum. Independent high-precision values for lambda=1/10,1/2,1,2,10 also matched the triaxial formula p4=1-p6.

originality.rationale: Direct mathematical coverage by two complete published 2026-10-11 results. The triaxial-octahedron theorem gives p6(a,b,c)=4/pi atan(2abc/D) for ALL positive orthogonal axis lengths, and uniquely maximizes it at equal axes. Restricting to (a,b,c)=(1,1,lambda) gives the audited full p6(lambda) law and strict lambda=1 optimum, including all lambda>0. Independently, the rectangular-box central-section hexagon theorem gives a complete all-side-length probability formula and the same rigid maximum. Polarity identifies the octahedron shadow with the polar of the central section of the reciprocal-axis box [−1,1]x[−1,1]x[−1/lambda,1/lambda] in the same projection plane, preserving 4/6 face counts. These are substantive prior mathematical implications, not merely similar titles. Both records are dated 2026-10-11, as is the assigned source, so this is a mathematical non-originality assessment and does NOT assert chronological priority, authorship, derivation, or copying. The auxiliary all-affine twelve-cone identity is expressly a proof device, a direct generic angle partition, and not a surviving separately motivated main novelty claim.
